newsitem.title: USA: RBNZ's Brash sees support for stable prices policy.
newsitem.headline: RBNZ's Brash sees support for stable prices policy.

text.p: Donald Brash, governor of the Reserve Bank of New Zealand, on Friday said he sees strong support for his country's law that requires the central bank to seek low inflation as its key objective.

"Market research commissioned by the Bank recently suggested that 63 percent of the public were aware that delivering low inflation was the Bank's key objective, and 73 percent were in favor of that objective," Brash said in a paper he delivered to a symposium here that is being sponsored by the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City.

Brash pointed out that within the business and farming communities there are some groups under pressure from weak commodity prices who have asked whether there might be non- monetary means of curbing inflation.
"However," Brash added, "almost unanimously, those same people are very quick to reject any thought of a return to the days of high and variable inflation.
